newsitem.title: CANADA: Biochem slips on lamivudine study results.
newsitem.headline: Biochem slips on lamivudine study results.

text.p: Shares of BioChem Pharma Inc slipped in brisk trading on Thursday after the company and Glaxo Wellcome Plc released clinical trial results on lamivudine, a new drug for the treatment of Hepatitis B.
On Nasdaq, where Montreal-based Biochem Pharma's stock is the most active, its shares were off 1.50 to 23 on a volume of more than 682,000 shares.
On the Toronto Stock Exchange, BioChem shares were down 1.70 to 32.55 on volume of only 570 shares.
By contrast, shares of Glaxo Wellcome, which licensed lamivudine from BioChem Pharma in 1990, climbed 23 1/2 pence to 11.13 pounds (US$18.04) in early afternoon trading in London.
In a joint statement in London, Glaxo and BioChem Pharma said advanced studies showed that lamivudine may reduce and even reverse damage to the liver caused by the Hepatitis B virus.

The companies told the European Association for the Study of the Liver that phase III clinical tests of lamivudine on 358 people with chronic Hepatitis B in Taiwan, Singapore and Hong Kong were "extremely encouraging."

They said 67 percent of patients who took a 100 milligram lamivudine tablet every day for a year saw the condition of their livers improve, compared with 30 percent who took a placebo. The number of people whose liver deteriorated was greatly reduced.
The companies said researchers also found that 16 percent of people taking the drug managed to stop the Hepatitis B virus from replicating in the blood, compared with four percent who took a placebo.
Analysts said BioChem Pharma's share price may have declined because questions remain about how effective lamivudine might be against Hepatitis B.
"The data were not stunning," said Edmund Debler, of securities research firm Mehta and Isaly in New York.
Debler said it was unclear from the study results whether lamivudine actually clears Hepatitis B from the body.
"You might need to take this drug on a chronic basis, so coming off the drug would just cause a rebound effect," Debler said. "We need much more data," he said.
More clinical trial results on lamivudine are expected toward the end of this year.
BioChem Pharma and Glaxo are also facing competition from other major drug companies that are developing products for the treatment of Hepatitis B.
